content: ESA Director General’s Office -------- Distribution: All staff ESA/ADMIN/ IPOL - WORK (20 1 7 ) 01 Paris, 14 March 2017 ( Original: E nglish ) ESA Unclassified – Releasable to the Public Corporate Policy on Benefits Offered to Staff Members by Exte rnal Entities 1 . INTRODUCTION It is recalled that Staff Rule 3.1/2 stipulates that “ staff member s may not accept from government delegates or firms maintaining relations with the Agency any gifts, gratifications or advantages that might affect their ind ependence or lead to doubts as to their professional integrity”. However, “inexpensive publicity gifts” may be accepted. This is also reflected in article 4.2 of the ESA Charter of Values. In the context of their work, staff member s are occasionally offere d Benefits by external entities. In view of the Agency’s extensive procurement activities and staff member s’ status as international civil servants and in order to preserve the Agency’s impartiality and independence, the following policy and its associated principles have been established in consultation with the Agency’s Staff Association so as to enable staff member s to determine the administrative steps to be taken when offered Benefits. All staff members in receipt of Benefits offered by external entit ies shall conform fully to this policy, its principles and its associated procedure. 2. P OLICY In order to preserve the A

P OLICY In order to preserve the Agency’s interests and the independence of its staff member s, it is the Agency’s policy to : i. define the principles which govern the conditions under which staff member s may accept or not Benefits offered to them by external entities; and, ii. establish the procedure to be followed by s taff members when offered such Benefits. 3. S COPE The present policy covers any Benefit(s) offered to a s taff member by an external entity with the exceptions of i nexpensive offers to participate at events taking place on an ESA site and hosted by an external entity, e.g. Christmas events. 2017-0431 ESA/ADMIN/IPOL - WORK(2017)01 Page 2 4. DEFINITIONS Benefits : For the purpose of this policy B enefits compr ise any gifts, gratifications and advantages whatever their nature. Economic Operator : Any natural or legal person or public entity or group of such persons and/or bodies which offers on the market, respectively, the delivery of supplies, products or serv ices . Expensive Benefit : A B enefit the value of which is 100 euros or more . Inexpensive Benefit : A B enefit the value of which is below 100 euros. Subcontractor : An economic operator who is under contract to a contractor of the Agen

the value of which is 100 euros or more . Inexpensive Benefit : A B enefit the value of which is below 100 euros. Subcontractor : An economic operator who is under contract to a contractor of the Agency to provide supplies or services in support of a contract placed by the Agency . 5. PRINCIPLES 1 5.1 Threshold The threshold for considering a Benefit as expensive is set at the value of 100 euros. The threshold covers both one single Benefit and the cumulated value within a p eriod of twelve ( 12 ) consecutive months of several Benefits relating to the same external source. Different subsidiaries of the same group are considered to be of the same external source. 5.2 Benefits in the form of financial instruments Irrespective of its value, any Benefit in the form of a financial instrument (e.g. payments, securities, loans, etc.) must be refused immediately by the staff member who must report it to his immediate supervisor without delay. 5.3 Benefits offered by Economic Operators s upplying goods and services to the Agency Irrespective of its value, any Benefit offered by an Economic Operator (including Subcontractors), in his respective field of expertise, who supplies goods and services to the Agency must be refused immediately by the staff member who must report it to his immediate supervisor without delay provided the staff member was aware of the contractual relationship betw

The procedural requirement for the declaration of invitations on mission claims, e.g. for restaurant meals , does not dispense staff members from the above mentioned obligation of notification. 1 Th ese principles shall also be made applicable to on - site contractors E SA/ADMIN/IPOL -WORK(2017)01 Page 3 5.5 Estimation of the value of a Benefit The staff member estimates the value under his own responsibility. In case of doubt as to the value or the appropriateness of accepting the Benefit, the staff member shall proceed as in the case of Expensive Benefits ( see section 5.7 below). 5.6 Acceptance of Inexpensiv e Benefits A staff member offered an Inexpensive Benefit may accept it without obtaining the approval of or reporting it to the Agency except in the cases of inexpensive invitations which require notification to th

taff member offered an Inexpensive Benefit may accept it without obtaining the approval of or reporting it to the Agency except in the cases of inexpensive invitations which require notification to the immediate supervisor ( see section 5.4 above). 5.7 Acceptance of Expensive Benefits Should a Benefit (including invitations) exceed the value of 100 euros, a staff member may only accept it after having been authorised to do so by the Department in charge of personnel matters . The request fo r authorisation by the Department in charge of personnel matters is to be submitted in writing with the approval of the staff member ’s hierarchy and shall explain the nature and strength of the relationship with the external entity. Should the Department in charge of personnel matters consider that the Benefit offered might affect the Agency’s interests or the staff member ’s independence or lead to doubts as to the staff member ’s professional integrity, it shall where relevant consult the pertaining service s prior to taking its decision. 5.8 Returning of a Benefit In cases where a staff member is not authorised to accept a Benefit, he shall hand over the latter to the Department in charge of personnel matters who shall return the Benefit to the external entity on behalf of the Agency or donate it to charity. 6 . ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES 6.1 The Director responsible for person nel matters is responsible for ensuring the overall implementation of this policy and its monitoring. 6.2 Directors and Heads of Serv ices reporting directly to the Director General are responsible for ensuring the correct implementation of this policy within their respective Directorates and Services. 6.3 The Head of the Procurement Department is responsible for ensuring that in the fr ame of on - site contractor support contracts let by the Agency , the latter contain the necessary provisions informing the other party(ies) of the principles established under the present instruction and of any resulting contractual sanctions in case of brea ch of said principles by the other party (ies) . 7. content: ESA UNCLASSIFIED – Releasable to the Public Page 1 / 9 ESA Corporate Social Responsibility Code of Conduct The European Space Agency is committed to social and environmental responsibility and ethical business conduct in all aspects of its activities. This commitment is clearly reflected in the ESA Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) Principles adopted in 202 0, which the current document builds on, as well as numerous internal policies applicable to ESA workforce. The provisions of this CSR Code of Conduct (hereinafter the Code) represent the social responsibility commitments of ESA itself as well as the expectations that ESA has for its suppliers. ESA expects its suppliers to identify risks and actual or potential adverse impacts that their or their suppliers’ activities may have on human rights, the environment or ethical business conduct. Where such risks or adverse impacts are identified, ESA fur ther expects its suppliers to reduce such risks to a minimum and that any adverse impacts, either directly caused or indirectly contributed to, are remedied. Compliance with Law ESA suppliers are expected to comply with all laws and regulations applicable in each country where they are established or operating, including all locations where they conduct business activities. This includes, among others, compliance with all relevant health and safety, security, environmental, social, and labour law provisions as well as anti - corruption and anti - trust laws applicable to them. This includes re spect of human rights derived from the Universal Declaration of Human Rights , the principles established in the International Labour Organisation’s (ILO) Declaration on Fundamental Principles and Rights at Work , but also extends further to providing fair a nd dignified working conditions as described in particular below. No child labour ESA expects its suppliers to ensure that no child labour is used in the performance of work within their organisation. The term ‘child’ is to be understood as a person under the minimum legal age for employment in the country where the work is performed, o r in accordance with the definition of the legal minimum age established in the ILO Minimum Age Convention of 1973 , whichever is higher. No forced labour ESA expects its suppliers to adhere to the laws prohibiting all forms of modern slavery, including forced or compulsory labour, human trafficking, bonded or indentured labour, and to prevent any involvement in such practices. ESA expects suppliers to provide all workers with a written contract in a language they understand, clearly indicating their rights and responsibilities with regard to wages, working hours, benefits and other working and employment conditions. Suppliers are expected to follow the ILO’s general principles and operational guidelines for fair recruitment and not charge workers recruitment fees, as defined therein, as a precondition of work. ESA UNCLASSIFIED – Releasable to the Public Page 4 / 9 ESA expects its suppliers to maintain high standards of physical, mental, and social well - being for its workers through relevant prevention measures and training. Wage, benefits and working hours ESA expects its suppliers to pay their workers at regular intervals at least the minimum compensation required under local law, as well as to provide all locally mandated benefits. Deductions from wages are permitted only insofar as they are mandated by local law, regulations or collective agreements and communic ated to the workers beforehand. PRINCIPLES OF PERSONAL DATA PROTECTION ( adopted by ESA Council on 13 June 2017 ) The main principle is the protection by the Agency of personal data and data subjects, in particular staff members and contractor personnel, with regard to the processing of personal data. Subsequent Policy and rules shall set forth the specific framework on : 1. Personal Data quality The Policy shall provide data quality conditions, including on accuracy and update of personal data. It shall also set the conditions related to the erasure, rectification, completion and amendment of personal data. 2. Processing of Personal Data The Policy shall detail the conditions of processing of Personal Data (e.g. collection, recording, disclosure, deletion, etc.) for fair, specified and legitimate purposes, in not excessive manners and in conditions protecting confidentiality, integrity and security

Personal Data security The Policy shall require that appropriate measures must be taken against the risks of loss as well as against unauthorised access, destruction, use, modification or disclosure of personal data, in particular when such risks concern sensitive personal data . Processing of personal data on behalf of the Agency The Agency shall assign the responsibility of processing of personal data to a third party data processor only if the latt er provides adequate warranties of compliance with the level of protection of the personal data set forth by the Policy as well as in the applicable procedures, and takes commitments consistent therewith.
